translation_notes: the region reads two names bound elsewhere in the enclosing test method (`root`, an ElementTree; `expected_data`, an accumulator dict): restored per AGENT_BATCH.md's kind:statement note, identically in original.py and translated.ldpy (translated.ldpy also imports rdflib for the wrapped call).

`rdflib.Literal(elem.text)` -> `f{rdflib.Literal(elem.text)}`. elem.text is a str or None (an empty element, `<X/>`), and the original turns None into the literal "None" (rdflib's Literal(None)). The language's coercion does not: `f{elem.text}` raises TypeError on None in ldpy 0.7.1 (None is not an RDF term), so the bare form is not the same program; the Literal() call has to stay inside the island, where f{ } only passes an existing term through. The island adds nothing here -- the stratum's clean case (`f{x}` for a str) does not hold when the value may be None -- hence `awkward`.

kept `root.iter(".//Viscoelastic//MeasurementMode")` byte-for-byte: ElementTree's .iter() matches an exact tag, not an XPath, so this is a pre-existing bug in the source repository, not something to fix (no refactoring). Built the fixture tree with ET.Element(...) instead of parsing XML text, so an element's .tag can hold that literal string with slashes (real XML forbids it) and the site actually executes over several matches plus a non-matching neighbour.

driver.py runs a second phase on copies of both files whose matching elements carry the texts None, "", "  " and a non-ASCII string; Literal(None) must give "None" on both sides, and "" must stay a (empty) literal.
